data.description:
## Description

**What**: Extend the reviewer-findings schema with a `verification_evidence: {command, output}` sibling field to `cited_excerpt`. Implement schema validation requiring this field on findings whose claim text matches the absence-language pattern set.

**Why**: Invalid reviewer findings citing absent symbols or missing files cannot be verified without evidence. The schema extension creates the evidentiary anchor the verifier agent (S3) needs to confirm or refute absence claims.

**Scope**:
- IN: Schema field definition in `plugins/dso/docs/contracts/reviewer-findings.md`; validation logic at schema boundary; expanded synonym anchor list (canonical + 13 reviewer-rephrasing variants); soft-deprecation enforcement (warn, not reject) until plugin cache version marker is present; version-marker-gated hard enforcement; documentation of the version-marker name, location, and detection logic
- OUT: Reviewer agent prompt updates (S2), verifier agent (S3), dispatch wiring (S4, S5), feature flag (S6)

## Done Definitions

- When this story is complete, `plugins/dso/docs/contracts/reviewer-findings.md` defines `verification_evidence: {command: string, output: string}` as a sibling of `cited_excerpt`, with schema validation requiring the field on every finding whose claim text matches the absence-language pattern set (canonical triggers: undefined / missing / does not exist / not defined / not found; plus 13 reviewer-rephrasing variants: unable to locate / appears to be absent / no implementation / no definition visible / cannot find / cannot be found / has no corresponding / has no definition / no [X] visible / is called but [no/has no])
  ← Satisfies: "Reviewer-findings schema extends cited_excerpt with a sibling verification_evidence field"
- When this story is complete, enforcement operates in soft-deprecation mode by default: missing field on absence-tagged findings logs a warning to review output but does not reject; hard rejection activates only when the consuming project's plugin cache version marker file (documenting its name, path, and detection logic) is present
  ← Satisfies: "Schema validation requires verification_evidence on absence-claim findings; enforcement applies in soft-deprecation mode initially"
- When this story is complete, the plugin cache version marker name, location, and detection logic are documented; S2 behavioral fixtures explicitly assert which mode (soft warning vs. hard reject) is active during their tests; S6 feature-flag-off regression path can establish a clear baseline against a known enforcement mode
  ← Satisfies: "Coordinated rollout" (SC1 versioning contract)
- Unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic

## Considerations

- [Maintainability] The expanded synonym anchor list must be stored as a single source-of-truth artifact (e.g., `plugins/dso/docs/contracts/absence-claim-anchors.md` or a JSON/YAML file) that both the S1 schema validator and S2 reviewer agent prompts reference by path — not duplicated inline in 10 agent files. If duplicated, agents and validator will drift when new variants are added.

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
data.title: As a DSO maintainer, the reviewer-findings schema includes a verification_evidence field required on absence-claim findings
